Creates a PlaceDescriptor, suitable for searching or retrieving rich data about a place.
Representations must have at least one member.
Arrays should be sorted with original and/or most accurate representations first.
- Parameters:
- representations: A list of ways to reference the place using common mapping concepts.
- commonName: Publicly known name of the area or place of interest. e.g. "Starbucks"
- supportingRepresentations: List of ways to represent a place that are proprietary or non-uniform
Returns a Boolean value indicating whether two values are equal.
Equality is the inverse of inequality. For any values `a` and `b`,
`a == b` implies that `a != b` is `false`.
- Parameters:
- lhs: A value to compare.
- rhs: Another value to compare.
Publicly known name of the area or place of interest.
Locations that do not have a public name (like a private residence) should be nil.
e.g. "Starbucks" or "Yosemite National Park"
An array of representations of the place using common mapping concepts
When searching or fetching a place from a mapping service provider,
the order of the list can be used as a hint. Representations that
most closely match the original data source come first.
For example a hike tracking app may include a `.coordinate` first, even
if an approximate `.address` is available. A contacts application may put
`.address` first, even if a `.coordinate` has been fetched for display on a Map.
An array of proprietary or non-uniform representations of the place.
If understood by the consumer, these can be used in place of or in addition to common representations.
